extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, bibliographers, editors, and researchers compiling or evaluating short-story publications and periodical rankings
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and conventions for indexing, classifying, and ranking short stories published in American magazines (Oct 1918–Sep 1919), including asterisks to indicate distinction, exclusion rules, notation conventions, and periodical-ranking metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk distinction system
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, and three asterisks are employed to indicate relative distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a one-, two-, or three-asterisk prefix on story titles to indicate degrees of distinction; the lists and tables presented are organized around these asterisk categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-asterisk criterion (permanent literary value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-asterisk stories are of somewhat permanent literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three asterisks entitle a story to a place on the annual 'Rolls of Honor'. (Verbatim: '"Three-asterisk stories" are of somewhat permanent literary value ... entitle it to a place on the annual "Rolls of Honor."')

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of reprints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All tables and counts of distinctive stories are computed excluding reprinted pieces (but see separate notes on translations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations are not uniformly excluded; some lists include translations and note when periodical rank is affected by translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The New York Tribune, The Pagan, and The Stratford Journal gain their rank chiefly through translations of foreign stories, and allowance should be made for this in any qualitative estimate. (Some lists explicitly state they 'exclude reprints, but not translations.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and timeframe of indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: All short stories published in the specified set of magazines and newspapers from October 1918 to September 1919 inclusive are indexed; some other periodicals (with only 'stories of distinction') are indexed as noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page enumerates the magazines included (American Magazine, Atlantic Monthly, Bellman, etc.) and separately lists periodicals indexed only for 'short stories of distinction'. Certain stories specially called to attention are also indexed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and indexing of 'short stories of distinction'
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain stories are labeled 'stories of distinction' and indexed accordingly (one-, two-, or three-asterisks prefixed to titles indicate distinction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-asterisk titles indicate more or less permanent literary value; one- or two-asterisk stories indicate lower degrees of distinction. The lists of magazines showing counts/percentages are based on these distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking metrics: number and percentage of distinctive stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodicals are ranked both by number and by percentage of distinctive stories published during the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables are provided 'BY PERCENTAGE OF DISTINCTIVE STORIES' and 'BY NUMBER OF DISTINCTIVE STORIES' showing rank order and exact figures (percentages or counts) for the periodicals examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-breaking method for periodical rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: Ties in the ranking lists are decided by taking relative rank in other lists into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If periodicals tie on one metric, their order is resolved by consulting their relative positions in the other ranking lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation: non-American authors, cross-references, and previous-index markers
rubrics_metrics.description: An asterisk before the name of an author indicates that he is not an American; cross references after an author's name refer to previous volumes of this series; '(H)' after the name indicates other stories by this author are indexed in 'The Standard Index of Short Stories' (Francis J. Hannigan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these markers consistently in the index to indicate nationality, cross-volume references, and prior-index inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical bibliographic references and pagination rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures in parentheses after the title of a story refer to the volume and page number of the magazine; in cases where successive numbers of a magazine are not paged consecutively, the page number only is given in this index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated convention for parenthetical citations so readers can locate the original items across magazine numbering schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviation conventions for periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: A standardized list of abbreviations is used for periodical titles (e.g., 'Atl' = Atlantic Monthly, 'Harp. M' = Harper's Magazine, 'S. E. P.' = Saturday Evening Post, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the provided abbreviations in the index entries to maintain consistency and compactness; the page lists many specific abbreviation mappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing exceptions and specially noted items
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain stories or periodicals are indexed only when 'specially called to my attention' or only for 'stories of distinction'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include some periodicals or individual stories selectively per the editor's note when they are deemed specially noteworthy, even if not fully within the regular scope.
